I have farmed these 10 mu in Quzhou County for 30 years, and I know every piece of this land. At 52, with seven people under my roof and some of the younger generation working off-farm in the city, I cannot afford big risks, but I also need cash for household expenses and my grandchildren’s schooling. This year, I will keep 8 mu in my wheat-maize rotation because that is the backbone of my farm—it gives us wheat for flour and maize for feed and sale, and I can manage it with the well irrigation I have. I will sow an improved wheat variety in October, use rotary tillage to prepare the seedbed, apply fertilizer at the usual rates, irrigate three times from my well, and spray twice for weeds and diseases. For the remaining 2.1 mu, I am planting spring potato. The buyer from last season paid a decent price, and my well can handle the extra water that potatoes need. Potato demands more potassium and more pesticide attention, especially for late blight, but I am willing to do three sprays because the income per mu is better than grain. After I harvest that potato in early June, the same 2.1 mu will go to summer maize, so all 10.1 mu will have hybrid maize planted in mid-June. I use no-tillage seeding for the maize to save labor and catch the season after wheat and potato harvest; one irrigation should be enough if the summer rains come on time, but I will keep water ready. I expect about 500 kg/mu of wheat, 2,000 kg/mu of fresh potato, and 550 kg/mu of maize if the weather cooperates.
